ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Points $P$, $Q$, and $R$ are the midpoints of $\overline{JK}$, $\overline{KL}$, and $\overline{JL}$, respectively. Find $x$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle JKL, with K at the lower left, J at the lower right, and L above. P is located on side JK, Q is located on side KL, and R is located on side JL. Segments LP, JQ, and KR are all drawn and intersect at point D. In the figure, on median KR, the part near D to R is labeled 28, and the part near K to D is labeled with a curved arrow as 6x + 23. Then reason: The problem gives that P, Q, and R are respectively the midpoints of JK, KL, and JL, so LP, JQ, and KR are the three medians of the triangle, and their intersection point D is the centroid. The centroid divides each median in the ratio from vertex to centroid : from centroid to midpoint of the opposite side = 2 : 1. On median KR, KD is the longer part from vertex K to centroid D, and DR is the shorter part from centroid D to midpoint R. Therefore KD = 2·DR = 2·28 = 56. Also in the figure KD = 6x + 23, so 6x + 23 = 56, 6x = 33, x = 33/6 = 5.5.

raw_record.question_text: Points $P$, $Q$, and $R$ are the midpoints of $\overline{JK}$, $\overline{KL}$, and $\overline{JL}$, respectively. Find $x$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as triangle JKL with P, Q, and R marked on sides JK, KL, and JL, and with medians LP, JQ, and KR drawn meeting at D. From the image, use the labels on median KR: segment DR is labeled 28 and segment KD is labeled 6x + 23. From the text, P, Q, and R are midpoints, so KR is a median and D is the common intersection of the three medians, i.e. the centroid. Apply the centroid theorem: a centroid divides each median in a 2:1 ratio, with the longer part from the vertex to the centroid. Thus KD = 2·DR = 56. Set 6x + 23 = 56 and solve to get x = 5.5.
